# Forward-Copy Lab Progression

Each lab is a **whole copy of the previous lab plus one new capability**, committed as a new
directory. Nothing is refactored into a shared module, nothing is deleted, and every intermediate
version stays runnable side by side. The repository is not a project with a history — it is a project
with **all its history checked out at once**.

Confirmed in `Information-Systems-Modelling`, which states the intent in its own words:

> "Read top to bottom and it reads like a build diary: each lab picks up exactly where the last one
> left off."
> — Information-Systems-Modelling/README.md, 2026-07-25

## The chain

| Lab | Directory | = previous lab, plus |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | `lab2/StudentService/` | (baseline) OpenAPI contract, generated interfaces, SQLite |
| 3 | `lab3/StudentService_vlab3/` | [[h2-database]] in file mode, an auth *contract* |
| 4 | `lab4/StudentService/` | AOP, validation, actuator, jjwt + BCrypt, uploads, profiles, an [[angular]] SPA |

Same package `pl.edu.pwr.tkubik.ism`, same artifactId, same `api → service → repository → entity`
split every time — see [[layered-architecture]]. The Java source count tells the story on its own:
**11 → 41 → 76** files, strictly additive.

Lab 3's README announces its one delta in its first sentence:

> "The skeleton becomes a real backend."
> — Information-Systems-Modelling/lab3/README.md, 2026-07-09

## What this buys

A grader — or a reader — can open lab 2 and lab 4 next to each other and see exactly what
authentication or AOP *cost*, because nothing else moved. Extracting a shared parent module would
destroy that: the diff would become a config change instead of a visible delta. For coursework whose
deliverable is *the demonstration of a technique*, keeping the ancestors is the correct call, and it
is the same reasoning as [[multiple-solutions-side-by-side]].

The numbering carries the order in the directory names rather than in a table of contents — see
[[numbered-stages-in-directory-names]].

## What it costs, measured

Copy-forward makes every earlier lab a fossil that nobody maintains, and this repo shows all three
consequences:

1. **Divergence goes unnoticed.** Lab 3's OpenAPI contract and README both promise stateless JWT
   auth; the lab 3 *code* has no jjwt, no BCrypt and no password check. The capability only becomes
   real in the lab 4 copy. See [[stateless-jwt-authentication]].
2. **Duplicates accumulate.** A 39-file pre-rewrite Angular scaffold sits nested inside the real lab 4
   SPA; `ontology.ttl` exists as byte-identical copies in labs 5 and 6; `instances.ttl` (557 lines)
   and `cardinalityTest.owl` are tracked and referenced by nothing. This repository is the corpus's
   four-way instance of [[keep-the-superseded-version-in-tree]].
3. **Fixes do not propagate backwards.** Nothing that was learned in lab 4 was ever applied to labs
   2 and 3, because they are finished artefacts, not living code. Per the interview the whole repo
   is "All finished and frozen" (2026-07-28), so that is a description rather than a complaint.

## Scope

Evidenced in **one repository**. The corpus-wide relative is the family of repos that keep
alternatives visible rather than replacing them — [[multiple-solutions-side-by-side]] and
[[numbered-stages-in-directory-names]] — but the specific move of copying a whole working
application forward and adding to it is, so far, particular to this coursework.
